title: The Educated Barbarian: Meditations analysis (part. 17)
summary: Episode 17 of NH's Meditations reading. He applies Marcus Aurelius to physique anxiety (focus on the present instead of fretting about future bodyweight), to sharing ideas without proselytising or tying your self-esteem to others' approval, and to fame, hedonism versus fulfilment in work, listening without projecting, community benefit, leadership by goodwill rather than fear, and living by your own principles rather than to please others.
claims: Worrying about how much you'll weigh in two years is anxiety about an unmaterialised future; focus on present training and deal with the future when it arrives
Share your ideas, but don't force them on others; conversion by force creates slaves, not believers
Fitness YouTubers who get upset when rejected have tied others' acceptance to their self-esteem; you should be able to leave a room of a thousand critics unscathed
If criticism makes you question your beliefs, revisit them; they may have been flawed
Worshipping celebrities is a parasocial attempt to share their status; reject fame and judge people equally by their actions
Never seek pleasure for its own sake; pleasure should reward hard work. Drugs, TV and junk food short-circuit the reward system
Once you find work that fulfils you, it stops feeling like work; on days off he works on other projects rather than lying on the couch
He admits being very judgmental, with an opinion on everything; detachment means not forming needless opinions
Most arguments fail because people filter others' words through their own interpretation and emotions; listen closely without projecting
What benefits the community benefits the individual; a gold mansion in a bad neighbourhood is worth nothing
Leaders who rule by fear eventually fall; liked leaders create a productive, virtuous circle
Confidence moves you forward; people who tell you not to be confident want you miserable or want to use you
Live by your own principles and don't do things to please others, which leads to transactional favours or resentment
Visualisation is useful for preparation, but don't mentally live out events before they happen
